slice.reason_for_selection: r289 explicitly selected the next strongest already-exposed connected write surface after Gmail. Google Calendar event creation is exposed and independently hosted, so it is a cheap falsifiable candidate for an external witness primitive without installing a new service.
observations: The exposed Google Calendar create_event action can create an event, but its contract says to use it only when the user explicitly wants a calendar event, focus block, hold, or meeting created; therefore unattended creation without current user intent is not established.
The connected Google Calendar surface explicitly supports create, update, and delete event changes, so the exposed event object is not append-only under the available action model.

The create_event schema exposes ordinary event fields such as title, start/end time, attendees, visibility, recurrence and reminders, but no cryptographic timestamp commitment, immutable audit root, append-only ledger proof, or provider-signed inclusion proof.

No calendar event was created because this slice is capability-contract inspection only and creating an external event merely to manufacture witness evidence would violate the action contract and the role continuation.

Rekor remains a strong independent read-only witness for preexisting entries but generic creation is blocked by signing identity/material plus external write-path requirements.

OpenTimestamps remains the preferred keyless external witness candidate because public calendars are free and require no registration/API key, but immediate witness creation still lacks a proven currently exposed generic external submission action.

Gmail send_email is falsified as a qualifying append-only timestamp witness because it requires user send intent/recipient and ordinary mailbox records lack cryptographic append-only public timestamp semantics.

Google Calendar create_event is now falsified for this leaf because its exposed contract requires explicit user event intent, the connected surface permits update/delete, and the schema exposes no cryptographic append-only timestamp proof.
